html:
Between 1755 and 1759 the Qing dynasty of China conquered the Dzungar Khanate, the last great nomad empire of the steppe, and destroyed the Dzungar people. Most historians call it a genocide.

The Dzungars, Oirat Mongols ruling from the Ili valley, had fought the Qing for some seventy years over Mongolia, Tibet and the oases. In 1755, with the khanate torn by fights over the succession, the Qianlong Emperor sent armies in, with help from the Dzungar prince Amursana. When Amursana rose against Qing rule later that year, Qianlong ordered the Dzungars wiped out. Qing troops, Manchu, Mongol and Han, killed the men and enslaved women and children, helped by Turkic oasis people who had suffered under Dzungar rule. Smallpox did the rest. By common estimates most of a population of several hundred thousand died, from disease, killing or flight.

The emptied land and the Tarim oases, taken in 1759, became the Qing territory later named Xinjiang, "new frontier", and were resettled with Han, Hui, Uyghur, Sibe and other colonists. The fall of the Dzungars ended two thousand years in which steppe peoples like the Xiongnu could threaten China.
sum: Between 1755 and 1759 the Qing dynasty of China conquered the Dzungar Khanate, the last great nomad empire of the steppe, and destroyed the Dzungar people. Most historians call it a genocide.
